translation_en: Abdullah bin Mughaffal said: We were besieging the fortress of Khaybar when someone threw down a leather bag of fat. I jumped to take it, then turned and saw the Prophet, so I felt embarrassed in front of him.

Rafi bin Khadij said, Messenger of Allah, tomorrow we will meet the enemy, but we have no knives. He said, Be quick, or use something that makes the blood flow and over which Allah's name is mentioned, then eat, except what is killed with a tooth or nail. A tooth is a bone, and a nail is the knife of the Abyssinians. We obtained camels and sheep as spoils. A camel ran away, and a man shot it with an arrow, stopping it. The Messenger of Allah said, These camels can bolt like wild animals; if one overpowers you, deal with it this way.

Asma bint Abi Bakr said, During the Prophet's time we slaughtered a horse and ate it. Asma's daughter Fatimah reported this from her, through Hisham bin Urwah, from his father. They slaughtered and ate the horse during the Prophet's lifetime.
Asma said that in Medina, during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, they slaughtered a horse and ate it. Asma reported this practice in Medina.

Asma bint Abi Bakr said that during the Messenger of Allah's time they slaughtered a horse and ate it. Waki and Ibn Uyaynah also reported the slaughtering from Hisham. Qutaybah reported it from Jarir, from Hisham, from Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma.
Anas said: I entered with him upon al-Hakam bin Ayyub. He saw boys—or young men—who had tied up a chicken and were shooting at it. Anas said, The Prophet forbade that animals be tied up as targets.

Ibn Umar visited Yahya bin Said and saw a boy from Yahya's family tie up a chicken and shoot at it. Ibn Umar walked over, untied it, and brought the chicken and boy back with him. He said, Tell your boy not to tie this bird up to be killed. I heard the Prophet forbid tying up an animal or anything else as a target for killing.

Said bin Jubair said: I was with Ibn Umar when they passed some young men—or a group—who had tied up a chicken and were shooting at it. When they saw Ibn Umar, they moved away. Ibn Umar asked, Who did this? The Prophet cursed whoever did this. Sulayman reported from Shubah, from al-Minhal, from Said, from Ibn Umar, that the Prophet cursed anyone who mutilated an animal. Adi also reported it from Said, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet.
Abdullah bin Yazid reported that the Prophet forbade plundering and mutilation. Adi bin Thabit heard Abdullah bin Yazid report the Prophet's prohibition of plundering and mutilation.

Abu Musa al-Ashari said, I saw the Prophet eating chicken. Zahdam described being with Abu Musa when chicken was served and a man refused it. Abu Musa reminded him that he had personally seen the Prophet eat chicken. He then told how a group of Asharis had asked the Prophet for mounts. He was distributing charity camels and swore that he had nothing to carry them on. Later camels came as spoils, and he called for the Asharis and gave them five fine camels. Zahdam feared the Prophet had forgotten his oath and returned with the others to remind him. The Prophet explained that Allah had provided the mounts and that when he swore an oath but found something better, he would do the better thing and make expiation.

Zahdam said: We were with Abu Musa al-Ashari, and there was a bond of kinship between us and the tribe of Jarm. Chicken meat was brought, but a reddish-complexioned man among us did not approach it. Abu Musa told him to come closer, saying he had seen the Messenger of Allah eat it. The man replied that he had once seen the Prophet eat something he disliked and had sworn not to eat it. Abu Musa said, Come closer and I will tell you what happened. He had come to the Prophet with a group of Asharis and found him angry while distributing charity camels. They asked him for mounts, and he swore he would not provide them. He said, I have nothing to carry you on. Later, some camels were brought to the Prophet as spoils. He called out, Where are the Asharis? Where are the Asharis? He gave them five fine, high-backed camels. After a short while Zahdam said to his companions, The Messenger may have forgotten his oath. By Allah, if we let the Messenger's oath pass unnoticed, we will never prosper. They went back and said, Messenger of Allah, we asked for mounts, and you swore you would not give them. We thought you had forgotten your oath. He said, Allah is the One who gave you mounts. By Allah, if I swear an oath and then see that something else is better, I do what is better and make expiation for my oath.
Asma said they slaughtered a horse during the Messenger of Allah's time and ate it. Asma reported this act during the Messenger's lifetime.

Jabir bin Abdullah said that on the day of Khaybar the Prophet forbade the meat of domestic donkeys but allowed horse meat. Jabir bin Abdullah narrated this ruling from the Prophet concerning the events at Khaybar.
Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet forbade domestic donkey meat on the day of Khaybar. Salim and Nafi reported this from Ibn Umar. This report concerns the prohibition issued on the day of Khaybar.

Abdullah reported that the Prophet forbade domestic donkey meat. Ibn al-Mubarak also reported it from Ubaidullah, from Nafi. Abu Usamah reported it from Ubaidullah, from Salim. Ibn al-Mubarak also reported it from Ubaidullah, from Nafi; Abu Usamah reported it from Ubaidullah, from Salim.

Ali said the Messenger of Allah forbade temporary marriage in the year of Khaybar and the meat of domestic donkeys. Ali reported that prohibition as applying in the year of Khaybar. The narrator is Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.
Jabir bin Abdullah said that on the day of Khaybar the Prophet forbade donkey meat and allowed horse meat. This is another report from Jabir about the Prophet's ruling at Khaybar.
Al-Bara and Ibn Abi Awfa reported that the Prophet forbade donkey meat. Al-Bara and Ibn Abi Awfa both reported the Prophet's prohibition of donkey meat.

Abu Thalabah said the Messenger of Allah made domestic donkey meat unlawful. Al-Zubaidi and Uqail also reported this from Ibn Shihab. Malik, Maamar, al-Majishun, Yunus, and Ibn Ishaq reported from al-Zuhri that the Prophet forbade eating any predatory animal with fangs. Abu Thalabah said the Messenger declared the meat unlawful. Other narrators followed Ibn Shihab with this report.

Anas said a man came to the Messenger of Allah and told him that the donkeys had been eaten. Another came and said the same. Then someone came and said the donkeys had all been used up. The Prophet ordered a caller to announce to the people that Allah and His Messenger forbade the meat of domestic donkeys, because it is impure. The pots were overturned while the meat was still boiling in them.

Amr said he asked Jabir bin Zayd about people claiming the Messenger of Allah forbade domestic donkeys. Jabir said al-Hakam bin Amr al-Ghifari used to say that among them in Basra, but Ibn Abbas, called the learned sea, rejected it and recited: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden. (Quran 6:145)

Abu Thalabah reported that the Messenger of Allah forbade eating every predatory animal with fangs. Yunus, Maamar, Ibn Uyaynah, and al-Majishun also reported it from al-Zuhri. Abu Thalabah narrated this prohibition. Several other narrators also reported it from al-Zuhri.

Ibn Abbas said the Prophet passed by a dead goat and said, Why did its owners not make use of its hide? Ibn Abbas reported this statement from the Prophet about the hide of a dead goat. The Prophet pointed out that the hide could be put to use.

Abu Huraira reported that anyone wounded in Allah's cause will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound bleeding. Its color will be the color of blood, and its fragrance the fragrance of musk. Abu Huraira reported this teaching about the wound of a person injured in Allah's cause.

Abu Musa reported that the Prophet said, The example of a good companion and a bad companion is like that of a seller of musk and a blacksmith blowing his bellows. The seller of musk may give you some, you may buy some from him, or you may find a pleasant fragrance from him. The one blowing the bellows may burn your clothes or you may find an unpleasant smell from him.

Anas said they startled a rabbit at Marr al-Zahran. The people chased it and grew tired, but Anas caught it and brought it to Abu Talhah, who slaughtered it. He sent its haunches—or its thighs—to the Prophet, and the Prophet accepted them.
Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet said, I do not eat the desert lizard, but I do not declare it forbidden. Abdullah bin Dinar said he heard Ibn Umar relate these words from the Prophet.

Khalid bin al-Walid entered with the Messenger of Allah into Maymunah's home. A roasted desert lizard was brought, and the Prophet reached for it. Some women said, Tell the Messenger of Allah what he is about to eat. They said, It is a desert lizard. He withdrew his hand. Khalid asked if it was unlawful. The Prophet said, No, but it is not found in my people's land, so I find myself disinclined to eat it. Khalid pulled it toward himself and ate while the Messenger watched.

Maymunah said a mouse fell into some clarified butter and died. The Prophet was asked about it and said, Throw away the mouse and the butter around it, and eat the rest. Sufyan said he had only heard al-Zuhri report it from Ubaidullah, from Ibn Abbas, from Maymunah, from the Prophet, and that he had heard him say it many times. Someone told him Maamar reported it from al-Zuhri, from Said bin al-Musayyib, from Abu Huraira.

Al-Zuhri said that if an animal, such as a mouse, dies in oil or clarified butter, whether solid or liquid, the Prophet had reportedly ordered that a mouse that died in clarified butter and the area around it be removed, after which the rest was eaten. This was reported through Ubaidullah bin Abdullah.
